mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in two consecutive monthly releases
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 5 out of 10 tightening episodes defined by the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months indicates weakening labor demand, which reduces corporate earnings and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 6 out of 10 such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) combined with a concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand, which depresses corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both show YoY decline in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 7 out of 10 demand-contraction episodes defined by the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates a persistent contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 5 out of 10 supply-contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 2.0% combined with a concurrent rise in the CPI inflation index above 4.0% signals a monetary policy lag and impending inflation surprise, which erodes real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 4.0% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 4 out of 7 episodes meeting the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 6 out of 10 tight-labor episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in real GDP (GDPC1) quarter-over-quarter growth above 2.0% coincident with rising housing starts (HOUST) signals robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ > 2.0% AND HOUST rising for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 5 out of 8 early-cycle expansion episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals a sustained supply-side recovery, which lifts earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of the monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 4 out of 6 supply-recovery episodes.
